description: Causal-theoretic visual attributes for architectural image characterization, grounded in perception science, biophilic design, and vision algorithms

attributes.name: Fractal Dimension (Box-Counting)
attributes.causal_variable: Fractal dimension D (box-counting), optimal 1.3-1.5

steps: Canny edge detection (sigma=1.0, auto thresholds)
Binary edge map extraction
Box-counting at scales [4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256] px
Linear regression of log(N) on log(1/epsilon)
D = |slope|

theoretical_warrant.theory: Attention Restoration Theory + Efficient Coding Hypothesis

key_refs.finding: Nature images cluster at D ≈ 1.3
D ≈ 1.3-1.5 preferred cross-culturally in fractals and landscapes
Universal preference for intermediate D across cultures

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: D in optimal range matches neural tuning to natural scene statistics, minimizing prediction error and supporting attentional restoration

attributes.name: 1/f Spectral Slope
attributes.causal_variable: Spectral slope alpha in 1/f^alpha power spectrum

steps: Convert image to grayscale
Compute 2D FFT magnitude spectrum
Radial averaging to 1D power spectrum P(f)
Log-log regression: log(P) vs log(f)
alpha = |slope|

key_refs.finding: Natural images have 1/f spectral structure
Preference for images with 1/f structure

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: 1/f structure matches retinal ganglion cell receptive field distributions, supporting efficient visual coding

attributes.name: Lacunarity
attributes.causal_variable: Lacunarity L(lambda), measures gap distribution at scale lambda

steps: Binary image from edge detection
For each box size lambda in [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]:
Slide box across image, count empty cells Z
Compute probability distribution p(Z)
L(lambda) = sum(p^2(Z)) / [sum(p(Z))]^2
Average lacunarity across scales

key_refs.finding: Lacunarity distinguishes fractal patterns with same dimension

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Low lacunarity (uniform gaps) preferred; indicates balanced spatial distribution, avoiding visual clutter or extreme sparsity

attributes.name: Edge Density and Distribution
attributes.causal_variable: Edge pixel density (% of edges in image) and entropy of edge orientation

steps: Canny edge detection (sigma=1.0, auto thresholds)
Compute edge pixel count / total pixels * 100
For each edge pixel, compute local gradient orientation (0-180°)
Bin orientations into 8 directions
Compute Shannon entropy of orientation distribution
Return both density and entropy

key_refs.finding: Moderate visual complexity (15-35% edges) optimal for preference

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Too few edges: boring, understimulating. Too many: cluttered, attention-demanding. Moderate density balances interest with legibility.

attributes.name: Correlated Color Temperature (CCT)
attributes.causal_variable: Correlated Color Temperature (CCT), measured in Kelvin

steps: Convert RGB to XYZ color space
Extract dominant illuminant color (white balance)
Compute CCT from x,y chromaticity coordinates
Use McCamy's formula: CCT = -449*n^3 + 3525*n^2 - 6823.3*n + 5520.33

key_refs.finding: Warm colors (3000-4000K) perceived as more pleasant/inviting
Melanopsin cells respond to blue light; cool light suppresses melatonin

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Warm CCT (3000-4000K) activates parasympathetic response, promoting relaxation. Cool light (5500K+) supports alertness and cortisol.

attributes.name: Chromatic Distribution (CIE Lab)
attributes.causal_variable: Chroma C (saturation magnitude) and hue distribution entropy in CIE Lab

steps: Convert RGB to CIE Lab color space
Compute chroma C = sqrt(a*^2 + b*^2) for each pixel
Compute hue angle H = atan2(b*, a*)
Bin hues into 12 sectors (0-30°, etc.)
Compute Shannon entropy of hue distribution
Average chroma across non-background pixels

key_refs.finding: Balanced chromatic variety (not over-saturated) preferred
Moderately saturated colors more preferred than highly saturated

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Moderate chroma (20-50) avoids both drabness and visual overstimulation. Distributed hues create visual interest without discord.

attributes.name: Green Chromaticity
attributes.causal_variable: Proportion of image pixels with dominant green chromaticity (G > R and G > B)

steps: For each pixel in RGB image:
Check if G > R AND G > B (green-dominant)
Optional: apply Excess Green Index (EXG) threshold: EXG = 2*G - R - B > 0
Count green-dominant pixels / total pixels * 100
Compute green hue distribution (range of green tones present)

key_refs.finding: Humans have innate preference for natural environments with vegetation
Green environments reduce stress and cognitive fatigue

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Green wavelengths (500-570nm) associated with vegetation and healing; presence of green reduces cortisol and promotes parasympathetic activation

attributes.name: Isovist Area and Properties
attributes.causal_variable: Isovist area (total visible floor area from a point) and occlusivity

steps: Identify floor/ground plane in image (typically lower 30-50% of architectural image)
Detect walls/occluding surfaces using edge detection and perspective
For central point in image, compute visible area (simplified 2D proxy):
Ray-cast from center in 360° directions
Record distances to first obstacle
Compute area of unobstructed region
Normalize by total image area for scale invariance

key_refs.finding: Humans prefer spaces offering 'prospect' (visual openness) without losing 'refuge'
Isovist area strongly correlates with spatial perception and wayfinding ease

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Moderate isovist area (0.4-0.8) provides balance: enough visibility to navigate and feel secure, without excessive exposure or isolation

attributes.name: Ceiling Height / Vertical Proportion
attributes.causal_variable: Ceiling height as proportion of image vertical extent and vanishing point analysis

steps: Detect horizon/wall-ceiling boundary using Hough lines
Identify vanishing point in perspective lines (if present)
Estimate relative ceiling height from vertical extent above horizon
Normalize by total image height for scale-free metric
Optional: Use 3D reconstruction (Structure-from-Motion) for metric height

key_refs.finding: High ceilings promote abstract thinking and freedom; low ceilings promote focused attention
Ceiling height influences creativity: high ceilings increase creative associations

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Higher ceilings (>2.8m) promote exploratory cognition and relaxation; lower ceilings support focused tasks. Biophilic optimum: balance between openness and enclosure.

attributes.name: Enclosure Ratio
attributes.causal_variable: Ratio of enclosing surface area to open space volume

steps: Identify floor, walls, and ceiling boundaries using edge detection
Estimate visible wall surface area from perspective
Estimate floor area (isovist or visible floor region)
Compute enclosure ratio = (visible wall area) / (floor area)
Low ratio (<0.8): open, exposed. High ratio (>2.0): enclosed, cave-like

key_refs.finding: Refuge (enclosure) reduces anxiety; optimum is moderate enclosure
Enclosed spaces with controlled prospect (e.g., window views) support stress recovery

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Moderate enclosure (ratio 1.0-1.8) creates sense of security ('refuge') while maintaining visual connection ('prospect'). Too open: anxiety. Too enclosed: claustrophobia.

attributes.name: Spatial Legibility
attributes.causal_variable: Metric: information entropy of spatial structure (walls, openings, visual landmarks)

steps: Detect major linear features (walls) using Hough transform
Identify openings and transitions between spaces (doors, archways)
Segment image into distinct spatial zones (room regions)
Count number of zones and junctions
Compute entropy of zone sizes: H = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)) where p_i = area_i / total_area
Low entropy: simple, clear spaces. High entropy: complex, multi-part spaces

key_refs.finding: City legibility depends on clear paths, nodes, landmarks; applies to interior spaces
Spatial structure clarity reduces cognitive load and supports navigation

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Optimal entropy (2.5-4.5 bits) provides sufficient structural clarity without monotony. Clear organization reduces navigation effort and cognitive fatigue.

attributes.name: Material Naturalness Index
attributes.causal_variable: Proportion of visible natural materials (wood, stone, clay, fiber) vs. synthetic (plastic, vinyl, metal)

steps: Segment image into material regions using color + texture
For each region, compute texture features: LBP (Local Binary Pattern), Haralick features
Train classifier on known natural vs. synthetic materials (or use pre-trained model)
Classify each material region as natural, synthetic, or ambiguous
Compute naturalness index = (area_natural) / (area_natural + area_synthetic) * 100

key_refs.finding: Natural materials reduce psychological stress and increase perceived warmth
Wood environments show lower cortisol levels than plastic-heavy environments

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Natural materials (wood, stone) trigger sensorimotor expectations and haptic memories; synthetic materials feel 'cold' or artificial. Optimal ~60% natural materials.

attributes.name: Haptic Expectation from Visual Input
attributes.causal_variable: Expected surface properties (smoothness, compliance, temperature) inferred from visual texture

steps: Extract local texture descriptors: LBP, SIFT, SURF for each image patch
Compute visual roughness: variance of gradient magnitudes
Infer material category (wood, fabric, metal, stone, etc.)
From material, infer expected tactile properties using learned associations:
- Wood, fabric, cork: high compliance, moderate warmth
- Stone, tile: low compliance, cool
- Metal: low compliance, very cool
Return 3D vector (roughness, compliance, warmth) on 0-100 scales

key_refs.finding: Visual texture activates somatosensory cortex; we 'simulate' tactile experience visually
Texture names (rough, smooth) activate tactile imagery networks

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Vision and touch are integrated in multisensory cortex. Rough, warm, compliant surfaces (simulated tactilely) promote approach and comfort.

attributes.name: Olfactory Expectation from Visual Input
attributes.causal_variable: Expected olfactory character (freshness, naturalness, staleness) inferred from visual cues

steps: Detect presence of vegetation, flowers, plants (green chromaticity + morphology)
Detect water features (blue/gray regions with specular reflection)
Detect wood/natural materials (from ATTR-M1 classification)
Assess air circulation indicators: open windows, curtain flutter, dust particle visibility
Infer staleness: presence of dust particles, closed windows, stagnant air visual cues
Aggregate into freshness, naturalness, and pleasantness scores

key_refs.finding: Visual context (green plants) primes olfactory expectations and enhances perceived pleasantness of odors
Odor pleasantness is strongly influenced by visual context

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Presence of vegetation, open air, natural materials visually primes positive olfactory expectations. Closed, stagnant-looking spaces prime musty/negative odor expectations.

attributes.name: Biomorphic Form Index
attributes.causal_variable: Proportion of curved contours vs. rectilinear; average boundary complexity (perimeter/area ratio)

steps: Detect major object/furniture contours using edge detection
For each contour, fit curve (spline) and line segments
Measure goodness-of-fit for curves vs. lines
Compute proportion of perimeter that is curved
Compute perimeter-to-area ratio (higher = more complex, organic shapes)
Exclude rectangles (walls, windows) which are structural, not decorative

key_refs.finding: Curved, organic forms reduce stress and promote preference vs. rectilinear forms
Humans have evolutionary preference for curved forms (avoid sharp edges as predator/threat markers)

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Curved forms mimic biological shapes (plants, animals); activate reward pathways. Rectilinear forms feel artificial/hard. Optimum: ~50% curves.

attributes.name: Water Feature Presence
attributes.causal_variable: Binary presence of water + measure of water surface visibility and animation (movement cues)

steps: Color-based detection: water is typically blue/blue-green or white/turquoise
Look for specular highlights (bright reflections) characteristic of water surfaces
Detect regular geometric shapes (aquarium tanks, pools, fountains)
Optional: temporal analysis in video—detect ripple/motion patterns
Measure visible water surface area / total image area
Return presence (bool) and visibility fraction

key_refs.finding: Water elements (real or simulated) significantly reduce physiological stress markers
Proximity to water (visual or auditory) associated with improved well-being and mental health

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Water activates parasympathetic system; soothing visual (ripples) and auditory cues reduce cortisol and promote relaxation. Evolutionary: water = survival/safety.

attributes.name: Biophilic Design Score (Composite)
attributes.causal_variable: Weighted composite of ATTR-F1, ATTR-C3, ATTR-B1, ATTR-B2, ATTR-M1, ATTR-S1, ATTR-M3

steps: Normalize component attributes to 0-100 scale:
ATTR-F1 (fractal): (D - 1.0) / 1.0 * 100, clipped to [0, 100]
ATTR-C3 (green): use directly as percentage
ATTR-B1 (biomorphic): use curved proportion as percentage
ATTR-B2 (water): 0 if absent, 50-100 if present and visible
ATTR-M1 (natural materials): use directly as percentage
ATTR-S1 (isovist): area_ratio / 0.8 * 100, clipped to [0, 100]
ATTR-M3 (freshness expectation): use freshness score
Return composite 0-100 score

key_refs.finding: Combination of nature elements (plants, fractals, water, natural materials, organic forms) produces synergistic stress reduction
Biophilic design integration > sum of parts; cumulative effect on well-being

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Multiple biophilic signals converge on same neural reward/relaxation pathways. Composite score captures holistic biophilic quality.

attributes.name: Figure-Ground Clarity
attributes.causal_variable: Contrast ratio (Michelson contrast) and saliency of central region vs. background

steps: Compute saliency map using Itti-Koch or similar model (or deep learning)
Identify high-saliency region (figure) and low-saliency region (ground)
Compute Michelson contrast: C = (L_max - L_min) / (L_max + L_min)
Measure figure-ground boundary sharpness (edge strength at boundary)
Return composite figure-ground clarity score

key_refs.finding: Figure-ground separation is fundamental organizing principle of vision
Clear figure-ground separation reduces attentional effort and increases visual comfort

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Clear figure-ground allows rapid visual parsing, reducing cognitive load. High clarity supports spatial understanding and aesthetic preference.

attributes.name: Symmetry Score
attributes.causal_variable: Bilateral symmetry score (left-right reflection) and rotational symmetry

steps: Detect vertical axis of potential symmetry (center line)
Flip image horizontally; compare to original using normalized cross-correlation
Symmetry score S_bilateral = correlation coefficient (0-1)
Optional: detect rotational symmetry (90°, 180° rotation)
Return bilateral symmetry score and any rotational symmetries

key_refs.finding: Moderate symmetry (0.4-0.8) preferred; extreme symmetry (>0.9) appears artificial
Symmetry processing involves fronto-parietal networks; moderate symmetry optimizes fluency without boredom

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Moderate symmetry is efficiently processed (fluency effect) and perceived as balanced/aesthetically pleasing. Too much: appears artificial or sterile. Perfect asymmetry: chaotic.

attributes.name: Sitting Affordance Density
attributes.causal_variable: Number and distribution of detectable sitting surfaces (chairs, benches, cushions, etc.) per unit floor area

steps: Identify furniture regions using color/texture segmentation or object detection (YOLO, R-CNN)
Classify as 'sittable' furniture (chairs, benches, sofas, stools)
Exclude tables, shelves, other non-sitting furniture
Detect floor area using perspective analysis or known camera height
Compute density = (number of sitting pieces) / (floor area in m²)
Return density and distribution heatmap

key_refs.finding: Visual perception of affordances (e.g., 'sittable') supports action and environmental comfort
Public spaces with abundant sitting (low density) paradoxically support more social activity than crowded spaces

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: Visible sitting options reduce fatigue perception and support longer engagement with space. Moderate density (0.1-0.5/m²) balances accessibility with openness.

attributes.name: Social Density Inference
attributes.causal_variable: Inferred occupancy and interaction density based on spatial layout (proximity of seating, visibility between seats, expected foot traffic patterns)

steps: Detect furniture layout and seating arrangement (from ATTR-A1)
Analyze seating orientations (face-to-face vs. parallel: supports vs. inhibits social contact)
Measure inter-seating distances and visibility between seats
Identify central gathering points vs. peripheral isolation
Compute spatial integration metric: average visibility from any point to all others
Infer expected occupancy from available seating
Return social density expectation (0-100 scale)

key_refs.finding: Distance and orientation between people (proxemics) structure social interaction
Spatial visibility and arrangement influence social engagement and crowding perception

theoretical_warrant.mechanism: High visibility/proximity supports social interaction but can feel crowded if density >60. Low density (<15) may feel isolating. Optimum: moderate social expectation (15-60).

metadata.calibration_note: Attributes marked cultural_calibration=true may require culture-specific thresholds and weightings. Others are assumed universal across human populations.
